html:
On 25 October 1983 the United States, with small forces from several Caribbean states, invaded Grenada. The operation, called Urgent Fury, came six days after the killing of Maurice Bishop.

President Ronald Reagan said he acted to protect American medical students and to stop a Cuban and Soviet foothold. Cuban construction workers fought, and within days the island was taken. Britain, whose queen was Grenada's head of state, was given little warning and objected, and the UN General Assembly condemned the invasion.

Elections returned in 1984. The invasion was the first big US combat operation since Vietnam and a moment of the late Cold War.
